claims.statement: Payments are opt-in via config.payments = true; when false or absent, no /stripe/* calls are ever made, preventing 404 errors on services without the stripe plugin.

canManageBilling is derived from user.team.role === ownershipRole where ownershipRole defaults to 'owner' and is configurable via config.ownershipRole to match the service's accountsConfig.ownership-role.

No token renewal happens after a plan change because @subscription is resolved server-side from the database on every request (SubscriptionVarResolver), cached only for the life of that request. An upgrade is effective immediately with no re-login.

The redirect back from Checkout races the webhook: Stripe sends the buyer back over the browser while the payment confirmation arrives via a separate server-to-server webhook with no ordering guarantee. waitForSubscription and waitForOrder poll with immediate first check, configurable interval, and timeout to handle this.

WaitTimeoutError is deliberately separate from ApiError so that 'you're not subscribed' (ApiError) and 'you are, we just haven't heard yet' (WaitTimeoutError) never collapse into the same error screen. Timing out is not a payment failure.

The cart is a pure client-side data structure with no server calls. Every function is pure and takes the lines it works on, returning a new array. The cart is localStorage-backed and framework adapters wrap the pure functions without reimplementing them.

Prices stored in the cart are display-only. The service reads unit_amount from its own catalog when building the Checkout session, so a tampered cart line changes what the buyer sees but nothing about what they are charged.

formatPrice uses Intl.NumberFormat's currency style to determine each currency's decimal digits, preventing the amount/100 bug: JPY has 0 decimals (¥500), BHD has 3 (BHD 19.900), EUR/USD have 2 (€19.90).
createCheckoutSession rejects with status 409 when the team already has an active subscription. Checkout does not do upgrades/downgrades; send already-subscribed teams to openBillingPortal instead.
openBillingPortal rejects with status 402 for a team that has never checked out, because the Portal has nothing to manage without a Stripe Customer. Route a 402 to createCheckoutSession instead.
grantLicense returns 'granted' (201) or 'already-licensed' (200), and rejects with status 404 (no such member) or 409 (no seat available), all distinguishable on ApiError.status.
getPlans requires no session — StripePlansService does not check authentication, so it is safe to call from a public pricing page.
getSubscription is not gated on canManageBilling — any team member can see their team's plan, unlike createCheckoutSession, openBillingPortal, and the licence functions.

toOrderItems strips names, prices, and pictures from cart lines, sending only productId, quantity, and options (as metadata). The service reads product details from its own catalog; options travel because the service cannot infer variant selections from the product id alone.

loadCart returns [] for anything it cannot parse and drops individual malformed lines. saveCart silently ignores storage failures (private browsing, quota). The cart survives localStorage being edited by hand or changed by a deploy.

All adapters track the team id (not the user object) to decide when to reload the subscription. This prevents reloads on updateProfile or acceptConsents, which re-run checkSession and replace the user object but do not change the team.

The cart is independent of authentication: it belongs to the browser, not a session. A shop that requires sign-in before adding to a basket loses most visitors. The cart becomes an order (which needs a config) only when handed to createOrder.

readOrderRef reads the fragment first, then the query string. The fragment is the recommended placement because it never leaves the browser — absent from access logs, proxy logs, and Referer headers — which matters because the order secret is a bearer credential.

The catalog and orders collection names are configured per service (stripeConfig.products.*-collection), not fixed. Every function takes the collection name as a parameter; the default matches what the service uses when it hasn't been renamed.

RhPaymentsService in Angular returns Observables for all methods, wrapping the core's Promises via RxJS from(). waitForSubscription and waitForOrder update the internal subscription signal when they resolve.

Vue uses a plugin pattern: createRhPayments(config, auth) and createRhCart(storageKey?) return objects with a store property and an install method. The install method provides the store via Vue's provide/inject, accessible anywhere via usePayments() and useCart().
React uses Context: RhPaymentsProvider and RhCartProvider wrap the app, providing usePayments() and useCart() hooks. Both throw if called outside their provider.

All adapters keep cart state and localStorage in sync within the same operation (not via a reactive effect/watcher), preventing a removed line from being resurrected by a stale storage read on reload.

The adapter contract section E defines 10 payments test scenarios (E1-E10) covering: no calls without payments config, subscription loading on auth events, team-switch reload, canManageBilling derivation with custom ownershipRole, 409 error propagation, waitForSubscription state update, and no reload on profile/consent changes.
